en: On the left, a drawer with coins lying still. On the right, a transparent pipe with running water and a piece of armor carried along by the current. If the tap is turned off, the piece stops, intact, and loses its shine.

The platform must give information that truly serves a purpose, that helps you decide and that can be checked later if there is a dispute. Information that exists somewhere but guides no one does not meet this duty.

It helps to show what was displayed to you, at what moment, with what prominence and through which channel. It also helps to show whether, the way everything was organized, you could understand what mattered in order to buy, to stay or to react.

You can ask the platform to correct the way it informs and make what matters visible, to present what it actually displayed and to restore what you lost because of the lack of clarity. Depending on the case, the failure can be treated as a defect in the quality of the information or as an abusive practice. It can even lead to the invalidity of clauses that go against what you had reason to expect.

A contemporary building seen in cross-section, resting on an earlier foundation that was already marked out and ready to receive its structures. The blue highlights the immaterial construction and the line reveals the continuity with the foundation. It is the same plot as in the illustration of the Immaterial Object of Consumption, now with the building finished.

The platform must keep what you bought accessible, understandable and preserved in what makes it useful. It can change the environment, because change is part of this kind of supply, but only within the limits of what is legitimate.

It helps to show that what you use depends on the platform's environment and how it delivers that experience. It also helps to show your concrete position in the relationship, such as what is in your account, what you paid and what it lets you do.

You can ask for the case to be handled under consumer law, with what you bought seen as an immaterial product. The company cannot escape this just by saying it provides a service or granted a simple license, because the service is precisely the way the product is kept working.
The platform must keep a minimum of verifiability. That means making it possible to know what was changed, when, with what justification and with what effect on what you use.

What helps are the essential system records, the history of the versions that matter, the records of the punishment and the minimum justifications. Together with the context data, this should be enough for whoever decides to understand the problem. Almost all of this is usually held by the platform, not by you.

You can ask that these records be preserved and shown, and that an expert examination, meaning a review by a specialist, be carried out on specific points. You can also ask for a check, based on the minimum clarity the platform owes, of whether the change or the punishment was legitimate. Depending on the case, there may also be presumptions against the platform, which make certain facts count in your favor when the records only it had are missing.

The platform must preserve, in substance, the role the item had in your experience. That includes what it does, the relationship it creates with other players and, when this matters to the law, what it means.
It helps to show what usefulness the item had before, what changed, what the concrete impact of the change was and why the compensation offered, if any, is not enough.

First of all, you can ask for the function to come back. That can mean undoing the change when it is technically possible, swapping the item for something equivalent or correcting the way the update was made. Money should not be the automatic answer. Depending on the case, the loss can be treated as a quality defect of the product or the service, which is the name the law gives to the problem that makes something less useful than it should be.
A hand puts back the missing piece of a mosaic, while a neat stack of coins sits beside it, within reach.
The platform must keep and show the minimum records needed to reconstruct what happened, because being open to checking is part of the legitimate way of supplying.

On your side, it helps to give a plausible account of what you went through, show how it fits into the game and gather what was within your reach. On the platform's side, it falls to it to present the records, histories, versions and technical justifications that matter for the case.

You can ask for the burden of proof to be distributed according to who has access to the evidence. Depending on the case, there may also be presumptions in your favor, which make certain facts count as true until proven otherwise, and a reinforced duty for the platform to cooperate with the evidence.
The platform must give an answer that matches the kind of loss. If what you lost was a function, the answer should aim at that function, and not only at an amount of money left over at the end.

It helps to show the link between the platform's decision or mechanism and the loss you suffered. It also helps to show that it is technically or institutionally possible to restore, undo, swap for something equivalent or correct the procedure.
A maze seen from above whose walls are pages of a contract standing upright and lit screens. At the only exit, a hand holds a stamp. The text becomes a wall, and the wall becomes punishment.
The platform must follow procedures you can understand, give a reason that can be checked, let you contest in a reasonable way and not treat you arbitrarily.
What helps are the records of the punishment, the appeal path that existed, the criteria used, the difficulties in undoing the measure and what it did to the continuity of your experience.

A figure in armor at the center of a circle of silhouettes. The armor's shine does not come from it, it comes from the gazes of the people around, which cross and light up the piece. Where no gaze reaches, the armor is dull.

The platform must make what was advertised match what is delivered. The promise, the advertised value and the costs that did not show up have to match the experience you get, including after the platform changes the game.

It helps to show what the sales environment was like, what advertising there was, what was highlighted and how the item was presented. It also helps to compare what happened afterwards with what was promised.

You can ask for the offer to be corrected and honored, for what you lost to be restored and for the misleading communication to stop. In some cases, you can ask for sales strategies that are incompatible with what is really delivered to be struck down. Depending on the case, the law can treat this as misleading or abusive advertising, or as an offer that binds whoever advertised it.

The floor plan of a shop in which every aisle, by different routes, ends at the same checkout. The hidden lines of the design, with the points of friction and the exit concealed behind the shelves, appear dashed.
When does loss become the routine of the service?

When several small things work together to take advantage of your fragility or to make your experience worse as the routine of the service. They are small frictions that wear you down, losses everyone already finds normal and manufactured urgency. They are also artificial scarcity, a lack of clarity that works in the company's favor and equivalences that shift as convenient.
What can the design of the service not aim at?
The platform cannot build the experience with an aim of exploitation that goes against good faith, transparency and balance, or that disregards what you legitimately acquired.

It helps to show that there is a pattern, that it repeats and how the pieces of the environment fit together. It also helps to show the relevant impact this has on your practical freedom of choice, on your understanding or on the usefulness of what you use.

You can ask for more than fixing one episode. You can ask for the paths of the service to be rebuilt, for transparency to increase and for the design to be corrected. When that design produces a pattern of harm that repeats, the answer can also reach the structure that reproduces it.

A castle made of server blocks above the clouds. Down below, people play, and each of their gestures rises like a brick that makes the castle grow. At the top, a single lit window holds the panel from which it is decided how much everything is worth.

The platform must use its exclusivity without turning it into a shield to hide everything, worsen what you bought or take away your access without reason. The balance between the company's rights and yours is struck through the social function, under which those rights also exist to serve the interest of society. And it is struck through the limits the Constitution places on whoever exercises private power.
It helps to show whether the restriction the company invokes is really necessary to protect the game and the work, or whether it is serving to shield the way it governs the environment.

You can ask for consumer law to keep applying. In practice, that can mean a limited examination of the records that preserves the secrets, and control over the equivalence of what you bought. It can also mean that the company respects the duties of adequacy, transparency and restoration. And, if the game is shut down, that the exit comes, as far as possible, with a transition, preservation or transfer of what you had inside it.

The platform cannot build the experience in a way that only it understands. The design of the environment has to respect good faith, which is the duty of loyalty between the parties, transparency and your real ability to understand what you are using.

It helps to show the path you took inside the game up to the purchase or the problem, what was highlighted on the screen and where the information went. The records that make it possible to reconstruct how your expectation was formed also matter. Dated screenshots, screen recordings and the purchase and confirmation screens help, because they show how the environment was set up, and not only what you remember.

You can ask for the problem to be treated as an issue of the environment, and not as carelessness on your part. If this dependence on the platform's signals is shown, reinforced duties to inform, to advertise clearly and to present evidence may apply. Depending on the case, the practice can be seen as abusive, as insufficient information or as deception by ambiguity or omission. Combined with other elements, this can even change who has to prove what.

A waiting room with occupied chairs and a clock on the wall. Under a closed door a strong light leaks out, and everyone looks at it. The light is regulated by a hand that comes through the gap in the door, the same hand that moves the clock's hands by a string.

A closed black box with a window cut into one corner, through which some gears can be seen. Not the whole box opened, just enough to see what changed. Outside, attached to the box, an open logbook, and more than one person can look through the window.

A two-pan scale with the same piece of armor on each pan, the one from before and the one from after, identical on the outside. The one from after is slightly duller, and its pan rises, because it weighs less.

A building in cross-section with stairs that only go down, doors that only open inward, windows painted on the wall, the emergency exit behind three locked doors and a corridor that leads back to the start. No sign forbids anything, and the design traps.

An empty plot marked out with stakes and string, covered in weeds, and in the middle of it the frame of a building starting to rise. It is an open frame, without walls, and at the top of it stands the figure in armor.

A staircase seen from the side, with side exits on each landing and a lit shop window at the top. The highest step is always just before each exit and never on the way to the shop window. A ruler leaning against it shows that the difference repeats, always in the same place.

An attentive person carefully reads a card covered in clear signs. The lens that gives the signs their meaning is on the other side of a counter, in the hand of the attendant, who does not lend it. Behind the counter, the same label hangs from two different objects.

The same problems, treated as doctrine. There are eleven situations, and each one says when the duty applies, what the platform must supply, what proof can be required, how the case is qualified and what consequence it may have. The legislation cited comes in full text, and fifteen chapters explain the regime for those who will work with it.

A soft, rounded cover with a smiling interface face, covering the corner of a table. The cover really does cushion, but marks on the floor show that the table moves forward a little each day into the path of whoever walks by.
A speech bubble held by the hand of the user, with an intensity dial, like a light dimmer, turned by another hand that comes from outside the frame.

A magnifying glass over four different screens, an assistant's, a shop's, a delivery app's and a customer service one, and under the lens all four show the same gear. Outside the lens, each screen keeps its own appearance.
